data.body:
=== FIXED: the inbound-assignee oracle now asserts THE PASS MINTED THE IDENTITY, and the fix is
mutation-checked. Test-tier only, as the earlier triage concluded. ===

WHAT WAS WRONG, restated precisely because it was two compounding errors, not one:
 1. `.assignee` IS NOT THE IDENTITY. Local tickets store the assignee as a BARE STRING on both
    deployments by design (`inbound_fields._assignee_matches` exists for exactly that reason),
    and the mint is ADDITIVE — `apply_inbound_records._ensure_inbound_assignee_identity:83-135`
    states it "NEVER changes the human-readable name extraction". This story's own plan said the
    identity is not a field on the ticket JSON.
 2. `ensure_identity_for` IS CREATE-OR-REUSE. The old oracle called it and compared its return
    to itself, so it minted the very thing it was checking for. Even with (1) corrected, that
    comparison is a tautology.

THE NEW ORACLE observes the identity REGISTRY across the pass through the READ-ONLY
`rebar.resolve_mapping` (returns `str | None`; never creates):
  * BEFORE the pass: `resolve_mapping("jira", "admin")` is None — stated as a SETUP assertion so
    a pre-existing mapping is reported as a setup problem, not as a product finding;
  * AFTER the pass: it resolves. That DIFFERENCE is the pass's work and nothing else's;
  * the resolved id `is_placeholder` — the mint's documented contract is a GHOST identity, and a
    non-placeholder would mean it adopted a real person's identity;
  * `resolve_mapping("jira-datacenter", "admin")` is None. The family is asserted in BOTH
    directions: a positive-only check would pass a build that minted under both providers and
    forked the namespace the epic decided DC and Cloud share;
  * `.assignee` is non-empty, as a SEPARATE statement, so "no identity" and "no assignee" can
    never be reported as one failure.

MUTATION-CHECKED, because an oracle rewritten for discriminating power has to be shown to have
it — and a green live run is consistent with a tautology, so the live cell cannot demonstrate
this itself. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_assignee_oracle_discriminates_5200.py`
(harness-free, 2 tests, green) pins both halves:
  * RED IS REACHABLE — `resolve_mapping` returns None on a store nothing has minted into, and
    still None on a second call (a lazily-creating implementation would return an id the second
    time and quietly restore the tautology);
  * GREEN IS REACHABLE FOR THE RIGHT REASON — driving the PRODUCTION mint
    `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity({"name": "admin", "displayName": "admin"})`, i.e. the
    function the inbound apply actually calls, with a DC-SHAPED user object (no `accountId`,
    only `name` — bug 5f48's exact shape) makes all three clauses hold. Calling the registry
    directly instead would have proven the oracle self-consistent while saying nothing about
    whether the DC path reaches it.

Placed in `tests/unit/` deliberately: a module under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` without a
harness skipif does not run harness-free — the autouse fixture burns the budget and errors.

NOT VERIFIED LIVE FROM THIS SESSION. I brought the Docker harness up on this arm64 workstation to
try; it reached "Starting the JIRA Plugin System" and then stalled, which is exactly what
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md:53-67` records as measured behaviour under emulation
("a native amd64 runner is a hard requirement for a run that completes"). The live verdict has
to come from the `ubuntu-latest` harness job.
